subject: general
question: Which of the following actions will permanently delete a file from an MS Windows system, bypassing the Recycle Bin?

options.text: Dragging the file to the Recycle Bin
Right-clicking on the file and selecting 'Delete'
Selecting the file and pressing Shift + Delete keys

solution:
The correct answer is __**Selecting the file and pressing Shift + Delete keys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dragging the file to the Recycle Bin:** When a file is dragged and dropped into the Recycle Bin, it is only temporarily deleted and can be restored later if needed. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Right-clicking on the file and selecting 'Delete':** This action moves the file to the Recycle Bin, allowing recovery unless the bin is emptied manually. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Selecting the file and pressing Shift + Delete keys:** This action bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes the file from the system. Once deleted, recovery is not possible through regular methods. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
